rationale: D gives the cleanest complete argument: it announces the planar/three-dimensional dichotomy early, proves the exceptional-pair and bad-triple estimates efficiently, and finishes with a particularly economical integrated mass contradiction. B is equally convincing mathematically and its named claims make the difficult endpoint argument easy to audit, though it is somewhat longer than D. A is also correct and highly explanatory, but its preliminary normalization discussion and notation around the integrated measure make the presentation slightly heavier than B's. C contains the same sound core argument, but it is substantially more diffuse and invokes undefined references such as \eqref{ang:direction-pair-kernel} and \eqref{ang:point-slice-total}, forcing the reader to reconstruct justifications that the other proofs supply directly.
